theme: wildcard: a regulator/compliance analyst tracking STR ordinances, regi
persona: regulator/compliance analyst tracking STR ordinances, registration numbers, enforcement data and DAC7 platform reporting across the EU, US, Canada and Australia
ideas: 1. EU DAC7 / OECD Model Reporting Rules for Digital Platforms (MRDP) — open-source XML schema implementations, national tax-authority reporting-portal clients, or compliance software that platforms like Airbnb file through. HIT-RATE: MISS — no 'dac7' GitHub topic exists yet and targeted repo searches returned nothing usable; genuinely under-built on GitHub as of Sep 2026.

2. City STR registration-number open-data git-scrapers (Toronto, LA HSO, SF OSTR, NYC OSE) that snapshot daily/weekly so a registered-listing count becomes a point-in-time time series. HIT — several Toronto repos found, one an actual daily git-scrape.

3. Legistar/Granicus municipal-agenda scrapers, usable to track STR-ordinance bills/votes/enforcement hearings across hundreds of US cities that use the Legistar platform. HIT — multiple mature scraper libraries.

4. Academic urban-governance lab repos that already run STR regulatory-compliance studies city-by-city (registration compliance rates, delisting after enforcement, commercial/ghost-hostel detection) — found via a Toronto STR registration search, not an 'Airbnb' search. HIT, and a big one — UPGo-McGill (McGill Urban Politics & Governance lab, David Wachsmuth) has ~30 repos: BC, Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Ottawa, LA, Prince Edward County STR reports plus an R package (strr) purpose-built for classifying commercial/ghost STR operations from AirDNA-format data.

5. Canada CITQ (Quebec STR licence number registry) trackers/scrapers. HIT — folded into idea 4 (UPGo-McGill citq-rapport-2024); noisy generic 'CITQ' search otherwise (unrelated repos share the acronym).
6. Vancouver/BC short-term rental provincial registry data pulls. HIT (weak) — one hobby Inside-Airbnb notebook, not the registry itself; UPGo-McGill's BC reports (idea 4) are the real find here.

7. Italy's national STR identification code (Codice Identificativo Nazionale, 'CIN') registry mirrors/scrapers — a 2024 law requiring every Italian short-term listing to display a CIN. MISS — GitHub search for CIN + 'affitti brevi' returned zero results (rate-limited on web search too, but gh search was clean and empty); worth a follow-up in Italian.

8. Amsterdam/Berlin/Vienna municipal short-term-rental permit or Zweckentfremdung registries as open-data git mirrors. UNTESTED/RATE-LIMITED — github.com/search hit HTTP 429 for both attempts; needs a retry by the next agent, ideally via `gh search repos` rather than WebFetch on the search UI.

9. Portugal RNAL (Registo Nacional de Alojamento Local) registry mirrors/scrapers, since Lisbon capped and later reopened RNAL registrations (a supply-side regulatory shock relevant to EMEA nights/ADR). UNTESTED/RATE-LIMITED — same 429 as idea 8; not yet searched via gh.

10. Australia state-level STR registers (NSW STRA Register, Byron Shire caps) as open-data pulls. MISS — 'STRA register Australia' search returned only unrelated repos matching on the word 'Australia'; no genuine hits found this pass.

candidates.name: city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration
candidates.what_it_holds: A daily git-scrape (automated commit at UTC midnight) of Toronto's official open-data 'Short Term Rentals Registration' dataset as a committed CSV (short-term-rental-registrations-data.csv). Because it commits a new snapshot every day, the git history itself is a point-in-time vintage series of registered-listing counts/IDs for Toronto going back to whenever the scrape started (repo updated 13 Sep 2026, i.e. actively running now).
candidates.why_useful: A daily, point-in-time count of legally registered Toronto STR units is a regulatory-supply proxy for one of Airbnb's regional mix components (Canada/NA) and directly serves CONTEXT.md gap #12 (city registration datasets) with something better than a one-shot snapshot — the git log gives vintages for free, addressing the point-in-time requirement in CLAUDE.md rule 2.
candidates.license: has a LICENSE file (type not confirmed)
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing daily snapshots from repo creation to present
candidates.size_hint: single CSV per snapshot, small; grows via git history

candidates.name: Toronto-STR-API

candidates.why_useful: Method-only: shows a maintained ingestion path for Toronto's STR registry (idea 2/gap #12) if the git-scrape repo above ever lapses.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only (no historical store visible)
candidates.size_hint: small API codebase, no bundled data

candidates.name: Toronto-Short-Term-Rentals

candidates.name: python-legistar-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: A Python library (BSD-3, 52 stars, updated Aug 2026 — actively maintained) that scrapes any municipal Legistar site: agendas, bill/legislation text, votes, committee actions, meeting calendars. Legistar/Granicus is used by hundreds of US city councils.
candidates.why_useful: A generic tool to build an STR-ordinance tracker across many US cities at once (introduction of registration caps, licence-fee hikes, short-term-rental bans/votes) — feeds CONTEXT.md gap #12 (STR ordinance trackers) and gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN-style open-data discovery is the analogue for civic legislative data). Method only, no data committed.
candidates.geography: any US city on the Legistar platform (SF, LA, NYC councils, many mid-size cities)

candidates.name: legistar-scrape
candidates.what_it_holds: Alternative, simpler Python Legistar scraping library (MIT, 23 stars) for pulling legislation/meeting data from Legistar-hosted city sites.
candidates.why_useful: Second, lighter-weight option for the same STR-ordinance-tracking use case as the opencivicdata scraper (gap #12).

candidates.name: sf-legistar-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: A Legistar scraper aimed specifically at San Francisco's council site.
candidates.why_useful: SF is home to Airbnb's own HQ jurisdiction and one of the earliest/most-litigated STR ordinances (SF OSTR, already partially held per CONTEXT.md); a city-specific scraper could pull ongoing enforcement/legislative actions rather than just the registry snapshot already in hand.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill (organization, ~30 repos)
candidates.what_it_holds: McGill University's Urban Politics and Governance lab (David Wachsmuth) — a running program of STR regulatory-compliance research with individual repos per report: bc-report-2022/2023-summer/2024 (British Columbia provincial STR registry law), toronto-report and toronto-report-2023 ('Analysis of Toronto's STR registration system', regulatory-compliance section, data/ folder, MIT), vancouver-analysis, ottawa-2021 (OLT ordinance hearing), pec-2021 (Prince Edward County), la-report-2021, montreal-finance-2022, str-ltr-mtl-analysis (STR units returning to the long-term rental market — a direct STR<->LTR crossover dataset, gap #13), citq-rapport-2024 (Quebec's CITQ STR licence-number system), commercial-operators, deceptive_str_operations ('Max's SRP' — detecting fraudulent/deceptive STR listings), and the strr R package itself (functions strr_FREH — frequently-rented entire-home listings, strr_ghost — ghost-hostel clusters, strr_multi — commercial multi-listing operators; built for AirDNA-format inputs, not raw data).
candidates.why_useful: This is a full academic pipeline for exactly the regulator/compliance lens the persona is tracking: registration-compliance rates, delisting after enforcement, commercial-operator and ghost-hostel classification, and STR<->long-term-rental crossover, across multiple Canadian and one US (LA) jurisdiction, with report-specific data/ folders and reusable R tooling. Feeds gap #12 (registration datasets, regulatory trackers) and gap #13 (STR<->LTR crossover) directly, and the strr package's FREH/ghost-hostel classifiers are a reusable method for identifying quasi-commercial (non-Airbnb-branded) STR supply that competes with or supplies Airbnb's own inventory.
candidates.license: MIT on most report repos; strr package licence not confirmed
candidates.last_activity: toronto-report-2023 and bc-report-2024 show recent activity (2024-2026 range per commit counts); org itself has current repos
candidates.geography: Canada (BC, Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Ottawa, Quebec, PEC) plus Los Angeles
candidates.size_hint: each repo small-to-medium (R scripts + data/ folders + Rmd reports); org-wide ~30 repos

candidates.name: strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (422 commits, in active development, not on CRAN) with functions to process AirDNA-format STR data and classify: frequently-rented entire-home listings (strr_FREH), ghost-hostel clusters (strr_ghost), commercial multi-listing operators (strr_multi), and to identify listings located in actual housing units (strr_housing) versus non-housing/hotel-like supply.
candidates.why_useful: A reusable, tested method (not raw scraped data) for separating 'professional/commercial' STR supply from casual hosts — relevant to Airbnb's own host-mix disclosures and to regional-mix/regulatory-exposure analysis; complements the Inside Airbnb panel already held by giving a peer-reviewed classification method rather than raw listing counts.

candidates.name: str-ltr-mtl-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Report and code on short-term rental units in Montreal returning to the long-term rental market — a direct measurement of STR-to-LTR supply crossover following Quebec's CITQ regulatory tightening.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses CONTEXT.md gap #13 (STR<->LTR crossover / host-supply economics) with an actual measured event (regulation-driven delisting into the LTR market) rather than a proxy.

candidates.name: toronto-report-2023
candidates.what_it_holds: Full Toronto STR/MTR (mid-term rental) report repo with R code, a data/ folder, and Rmd sections including 'regulatory compliance', 'COVID-related returning listings', and market overview.
candidates.why_useful: A finer-grained, peer-reviewed alternative/complement to the raw Toronto registration CSV scrapers above — gives compliance-rate framing directly (what fraction of active listings are actually registered), which is the regulator-analyst's core question and speaks to true North America STR supply versus what shows as 'compliant'.

candidates.name: bc-report-2024
candidates.what_it_holds: R scripts and outputs analyzing British Columbia's provincial short-term-rental registry law (BC introduced a province-wide principal-residence STR requirement and registration system in 2024) — likely covering registration/compliance rates and delisting patterns.
candidates.why_useful: BC's 2024 STR law was one of the most aggressive North American regulatory shocks to STR supply; this is a direct, academically-produced measurement of its effect, useful for the Canada component of NA regional mix and as an analogue for how other jurisdictions' registration laws might bite.

candidates.name: deceptive_str_operations
candidates.what_it_holds: R/Rmarkdown code ('Max's SRP') analyzing deceptive short-term-rental operations — likely listings that misrepresent registration status, host identity, or property count to evade local ordinances.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme for a compliance analyst: measures the scale of non-compliant/evasive STR supply, which affects how much of the addressable STR market any registration crackdown can actually capture — relevant to forecasting the effect of new ordinances on Airbnb's regional listing counts.
candidates.last_activity: 41 commits, README blank (thin documentation, would need code read to confirm geography/dataset)
candidates.geography: unconfirmed (likely Canadian city per lab's usual scope)

candidates.why_useful: Dependency needed to actually run any of the above UPGo-McGill report repos; catalogued for completeness/reproducibility, not independently a data source.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: supporting tool for UPGo-McGill entries above, not a new dataset on its own

candidates.what_it_holds: Toronto Open Data STR-registration analysis with inputs/outputs/scripts folders, examining which of Toronto's 25 wards have the most registered STR units and the tenant/landlord implications.
candidates.why_useful: A third independent Toronto registry-derived dataset/analysis, useful as a cross-check against the git-scrape repo and the UPGo-McGill Toronto reports; ward-level granularity is a finer geographic cut than the other two.
